items.title: The Lessons of Cancún, Fifty Years Later
items.summary: Cancún worked because Mexico found a market first and built the resort second. Most of its copies reversed the order.

items.title: UAE’s Hotel Divide: Abu Dhabi Holds Up While Dubai Sinks
items.summary: Dubai’s hotel economy runs on flights that haven’t come back. Abu Dhabi’s runs on an events calendar that didn’t need them to.

items.title: Perk Is in No Rush to IPO as Revenue Nears $400 Million
items.summary: Perk, the travel management tech company, says it can wait on an IPO as long as it keeps growing near 50% a year without burning cash. The choppy market debut of Navan, its closest rival, hints at one reason for its patience.

items.title: Lemon Tree Hotels Targets UAE, Thailand, and Maldives to Follow Indian Travelers Abroad
items.summary: Lemon Tree is betting a homegrown brand can find its own following abroad. But for now, it’s drawing the line at three hours’ flying time.

items.title: Inside GetYourGuide’s Sixteen-Year Road to Profit
items.summary: Sixteen years, about $750 million in equity funding, half a billion euros of losses, and one answer: repeat customers. Everything else was the cost of finding it.

items.title: Iceland’s Hotels Were Already Full. Then Came the Eclipse.
items.summary: The eclipse is expected to strain Iceland’s infrastructure, but tourism leaders are betting it can also convince travelers their next trip doesn’t need to be a summer stay in Reykjavík.
